title: Ziti al Forno
subtitle: Baked pasta tubes with a rich meat and tomato sauce
excerpt: Long pasta tubes layered with a slow-cooked meat sauce, mozzarella, and parmesan, then baked until bubbling. A proper Neapolitan Sunday bake.
sourceNotes: Neapolitan tradition. Ziti al forno is a centrepiece Sunday dish in southern Italy, typically made with a long braised meat sauce.

recipe.freezeNotes: Assemble and freeze before baking. Bake from frozen at 180C for 50 to 60 minutes until bubbling throughout.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The meat sauce can be made 2 days ahead and refrigerated. Assemble and bake on the day.

content.text: Ziti al forno is a Neapolitan baked pasta made with long tubes broken by hand, layered with a slow tomato sauce, mozzarella, and parmesan. It gives a deeply comforting, celebratory dish. The pasta must be slightly underdone before baking or it will turn soft.

items.prepNote: ziti; broken into thirds by hand
torn and left on kitchen paper for 15 minutes

content.text: Heat the oil in a large pan over a medium heat. Cook the onion for 8 minutes until soft and pale gold.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Pour in the passata and tinned tomatoes. Add half the basil and salt. Stir well.
Simmer the sauce uncovered over a low heat for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick and rich.
Heat the oven to 190C. Bring a large pot of well-salted water to the boil. Cook the broken pasta for 3 minutes less than the packet says. Drain well.
Toss the pasta with two thirds of the tomato sauce. Spoon half into a large roasting tin. Dot over half the mozzarella and half the parmesan.
Add the remaining pasta, the rest of the sauce, and the rest of the mozzarella. Spoon over the ricotta in blobs if using. Finish with the remaining parmesan and a few basil leaves.
Bake for 25 minutes until bubbling at the edges and golden on top. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

items.symptom: The pasta is too soft after baking.
items.cause: The pasta was fully cooked before going into the oven.
items.fix: Drain the pasta 3 to 4 minutes before the packet time. It continues cooking during the bake.

items.symptom: The dish is watery in the centre.
items.cause: The mozzarella was very wet or the sauce was not reduced enough.
items.fix: Pat the mozzarella dry before using. Reduce the sauce until it is thick enough to coat a spoon before assembling.

items.symptom: The top is browning too fast.
items.cause: The oven is running hot or the dish is too near the top element.
items.fix: Cover loosely with foil and move the dish to a lower shelf. Remove the foil for the last 5 minutes.
